label: Constitutional Analysis
sentences: The question here falls under Article II, Section 3. The President gives Congress information of the state of the Union and recommends measures to it; on extraordinary occasions he may convene both houses or either of them, and if they disagree about the time of adjournment he may adjourn them to such time as he thinks proper; he receives ambassadors and other public ministers, takes care that the laws be faithfully executed, and commissions all the officers of the United States.
This story is about sending monitors to check compliance with federal voting-rights laws.
In Federalist 69 (March 1788) Hamilton listed the duty "to take care that the laws be faithfully executed" among presidential powers that resemble those of the British king and the New York governor.
The DOJ claims about 1,000 election monitors are deployed in all 50 states.
The strongest argument against this is that stationing monitors across the states creates a general federal presence over local vote work and goes beyond only carrying out the laws.
We read this clause to mean the executive must make sure existing laws are followed.
Checking federal voting-rights statutes already on the books is carrying them out.
This keeps carrying out the laws with the branch set up for that work.

sources.label: James Madison, Helvidius No. I, Aug. 24, 1793
